clue.text: Former lover acting falsely is revealing

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
posing is pretending, putting on a false front

explanation.surface: An old flame's insincere performance gives the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing something means uncovering or disclosing it to view.

clue.text: Headless golf club giving slight advantage

indicators.note: a headless word loses its first letter, so the club's opening letter goes

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club with its head snapped off still gives a player a small lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge means holding a small margin of superiority over a rival.

clue.text: One being fussy about new necklace adornment

indicators.note: the fussy person goes around the letter for new, so it sits inside

parts.note: a pedant fusses over small details

explanation.surface: Someone finicky is fretting over a new piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant is an ornament hanging from a chain worn round the neck.

clue.text: High-Churchman?

parts.note: not a cleric of Anglo-Catholic leanings but a man who works high up on a church, repairing its spire

explanation.walkthrough: High Church is the ritualist wing of Anglicanism; read literally, a churchman who is high is a worker up on the spire.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplejack climbs and repairs tall structures such as church spires and chimneys.

clue.text: Fool, I note, upset with another fool

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: a twit is a silly person

explanation.surface: Someone calls another an idiot and is told the same in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I and N round to NI, then TWIT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a stupid person, a synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Trick created by cheeky fellow (the penny's dropped!)

indicators.note: the penny is let fall from the word, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A con worked by a cheeky rogue, with a cry of realisation that the penny has dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The penny's dropped' is an idiom for finally understanding, but here it literally removes P.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme or swindle.

clue.text: Team at sea against east Cheshire town

parts.note: the crew is the team that works a ship
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A ship's team runs into trouble off the east of the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is a town in Cheshire famous as a railway junction.

clue.text: Release one barge back on the ocean

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to emit is to give out or release
I is the Roman numeral one
to ram is to barge into

explanation.surface: A boatman lets a barge go and sends it back out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: EMIT + I + RAM gives EMITIRAM; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means relating to the sea and seafaring.

clue.text: Unpleasant matter hidden by being ungentlemanly

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the next words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words hold the answer

explanation.surface: Something nasty is concealed by a man behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is informal British slang for sticky, messy, unpleasant stuff.

clue.text: Maximum speed of prat: ego out of control

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vain idiot drives at full speed with his self-importance unchecked.
explanation.walkthrough: Prat is British slang for a fool; Top Gear was also a BBC motoring show.
explanation.definitionFit: Top gear is the highest gear of a vehicle, giving its fastest pace.

clue.text: Place to practise making plants — in snooker or gardening?

definitions.text: Place to practise making plants — in snooker or gardening?

parts.words: Place to practise making plants — in snooker or gardening?
parts.note: potting is sinking balls in snooker as well as putting plants in pots, and a shed is where either might be practised

explanation.walkthrough: A plant in snooker is a shot where one ball knocks another into a pocket; potting covers both the snooker and gardening senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A potting shed is a garden outbuilding where seedlings are put into containers.

clue.text: Unlimited happy medicine for chosen person

indicators.note: without its limits, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the inner letters of happy
an ointment is a medicinal salve

explanation.surface: A cheerful, boundless remedy is prescribed for the selected patient.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointment can be a person named to a post, the one selected.

clue.text: A victor breaks record, winning tennis tournament

indicators.note: the letters break into the record, splitting it open

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
V is Victor in the phonetic alphabet
up means ahead, as in one up

explanation.surface: A champion breaks a record on the way to taking a tennis trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davis Cup is the leading international team competition in men's tennis.

clue.text: An abridged motif for stirring song

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a theme is a recurring motif

explanation.surface: A shortened musical motif becomes a rousing tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is an uplifting song, often a national or rallying one.

clue.text: Vague problem making Chinese dish

parts.note: dim means faint or indistinct
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An unclear difficulty arises while cooking something Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Cantonese dumplings and snacks served in steamers.

clue.text: Site far off looking dry and sunny

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A location some way away appears to have fine weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair is a forecasting phrase for settled fine weather.

clue.text: Look briefly good with jousting weapon

parts.note: a lance is the long spear used in jousts

explanation.surface: A knight takes a quick, approving peek at his weapon before the tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to take a quick look at something.

clue.text: Hit a balding criminal perceived unfavourably

indicators.note: a criminal version of the letters is a corrupted, rearranged one

explanation.surface: A bald villain gets struck, which hardly flatters his image.
explanation.definitionFit: To be seen in a bad light is to be viewed with disapproval.

clue.text: Tree fruit's ace crop

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: An oak's nut is praised as an excellent harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut that grows on an oak.

clue.text: Lied about being lazy

indicators.note: about signals the letters being turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fibbed about being a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive or unwilling to work, synonymous with indolent.

clue.text: Get working security device, having been taken in by swindle

indicators.note: the device is taken inside the swindle, so it sits within it

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a lock secures a door

explanation.surface: A lock was installed, but the buyer was fooled by a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To clock on is to register arrival at work and begin a shift.

clue.text: Mob heard getting stash of riches

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken and sounds like another spelling

parts.note: a horde is a mob or crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd overheard talk of a treasure cache.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden store of valuables such as coins.

clue.text: Colour of writing fluid on page

indicators.note: in an across clue, writing fluid on page puts the ink after the page letter

parts.note: ink is the fluid used for writing

explanation.surface: Asking what shade the ink is on a sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pink is one colour, a pale shade between red and white.

clue.text: Foreign police officer sorted out danger ahead of me

indicators.note: sorted out means the letters are rearranged into order

explanation.surface: An officer abroad deals with a threat before turning to me.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police force.
